title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR original-stain syllogism — singular judgment
pass_a_gloss: GAR urges a syllogism: whatever evil is derived from Adam's first transgression into all posterity so that they do not begin to be before being affected by it, is from God's singular judgment as Supreme Judge punishing the preceding sin in Adam. But original stain is exactly such an evil. Therefore original stain is in all Adam's posterity by that singular judgment as punishment of Adam's first transgression—and imputation follows of itself.
pass_b_english: GAR. We urge this reason, &c. The evil which already from the time of Adam's first transgression is so derived into all his posterity that they do not begin to be before they are affected by that evil, is from the singular judgment of God, or from the will and counsel of God as Supreme Judge, for the punishment of that sin which had preceded in Adam. But original stain is an evil which from the time of Adam's transgression is so derived into all his posterity that they do not begin to be before they are affected by that evil. Therefore original stain is in all Adam's posterity by reason of the singular judgment of God, for the punishment of that first transgression of Adam; whence of itself follows its imputation.
source_text: GAR. Nos hanc rationem urgemus &c. Malum, quod jam a tempore primae transgressionis Adae in omnes ipsius posteros ita derivatur, ut non prius incipiant esse, quam illo malo affici, est ex singulari judicio Dei, sive ex voluntate & consilio Dei tanquam Supremi judicis in poenam peccati illius quod in Adamo praecesserat. Atqui labes Originalis est malum, quod a tempore transgressionis Adae in omnes eius posteros ita derivatur, ut non prius esse incipiant, quam illo malo affici. Labes igitur originalis inest in omnibus Adae posteris ex ratione singularis judicii Dei, in poenam primae illius transgressionis Adae; unde per se consequitur illius imputatio.
